context.guidance: Store Authentication Secrets with a current, salted, deliberately slow password hashing function, never with a plain or fast unsalted digest. Re-hash each existing record with the new function the next time the Data Principal authenticates. Rule 6(1)(a) requires protection of the Personal Data these secrets guard, and a weak hash removes that protection once the store is read.

value.fix: Replace the unsalted fast digest in the password setter with a salted, deliberately slow password hash such as bcrypt (cost factor of at least 12) or argon2id, using a vetted library, instead of security.hash(clearTextPassword). Do not roll your own hashing. Because existing rows were hashed with the old function, add a migration path: on the next successful login, verify the submitted password against the legacy hash, then immediately re-hash the clear-text password with the new function and overwrite the stored value. Mark legacy hashes so they can be identified, and force a reset for accounts that never log in again. Add a regression test that the stored value is not a fast unsalted digest and that two identical passwords produce different hashes.
